en.hubeali: Is’haq, from Abu Hashim Al Ja’fary who said,

‘I went over to Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> (11<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) one day and I wanted to ask him<sup>asws</sup> what I could forge a ring with in order to be Blessed by it. So I sat down and I forgot what I had come to him<sup>asws</sup> for.

So when I bade farewell and got up, he flicked over a ring to me, and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You wanted silver, so we<sup>asws</sup> give you a (ready made) ring. You profited the silver and the forging (of the ring). May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Bless you, O Abu Hashim!’.

So I said, ‘O my Master<sup>asws</sup>! I hereby testify that you<sup>asws</sup> are the Guardian of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and my Imam<sup>asws</sup> who Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Made a Religion by his<sup>asws</sup> obedience’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Forgive you, O Abu Hashim!’’.
en.sarwar: 21. Ishaq has narrated from abu Hashim al-Ja‘fari who has said the following.

“One day I went to see abu Muhammad (a.s.) and I wanted him to give me a certain amount of silver so I can make a ring out of it and keep for blessing. I sat down but forgot to ask what I had come for.

When was leaving and said farewell to him he threw a ring to me and said, “You wanted silver and we gave you and profited the gems and the cost of the goldsmith works. May Allah grant you blessings O abu Hashim.”

I then said, “I testify that you are the Wali of Allah, (one who possesses Divine Authority) and my Imam through my obedience whom I follow the religion of Allah.” He then said, “May Allah grant you forgiveness, O abu Hashim.”
